checks: Repeated debug/release named outcomes; compiled assertion mutant; exact restore; paired syntax
cost: O(T) ordinary descent plus speculative LHS parse/reparse; deeply nested indexed LHS probes can add repeated subexpression work, so no uniform linear proof. O(T) retained AST plus recursion depth; no nesting cap.
description: parse_program lexes then descends statements. Functions partition into Program.functions. LHS probing restores position when no assignment follows. Power is left-associated: 2^3^2 maps Pow(Pow(2,3),2); unary wraps power: -2^2 maps Neg(Pow(2,2)). Matrix whitespace before unspaced sign starts a new element; end is special only with positive index_depth.

inverse: The accepted parse relation excludes right-associated 2^3^2, flattening [1 -2] to subtraction, accepting naked end as expression, or returning a partially built Program on Result::Err. It does not exclude semantically invalid break, unknown function, public invalid AST or runtime division by zero.

P^-1(tree) contains texts sharing AST tags/literals and retained statement line/print flags; comments and many separators are ambiguous. For Pow(Pow(2,3),2), 2^3^2 is compatible; 2^(3^2) differs through Paren and tree shape. An evaluated scalar has much larger fibers.
limitations: Partial lexical syntax, no semantic proof or executable surrogate
Lexer-accepted token stream; recursive stack/allocation resources. No external files/evaluation. Function bodies may terminate at EOF/next function; ordinary blocks require matching terminator.
